propositions: Four deterministic, read-only metric functions derive code-health insights from git history and the working tree: module-size distribution against a single flat cap, cap-change events, churn (insertions/deletions), and refactor-to-addition ratio.

The cap is single-sourced from .github/module-size-limit.txt (no per-file ceilings); module_size_distribution scans src/rebar/**/*.py at a given ref against this cap and reports count, near_cap_count, over_cap_count, and max_loc.
cap_change_events parses git log over .github/module-size-limit.txt to extract limit changes as [{commit, old_limit, new_limit}]; a range with no changes returns [] (list, not Unavailable).
churn and refactor_to_addition_ratio derive from git log --numstat; refactor_to_addition_ratio returns None when insertions total to 0 to avoid ZeroDivisionError, else returns deletions/insertions.
All four metrics are registered into the c085 registry via single-arg compute adapters that extract repo_root/since/until from the evaluation context.

Tests verify exact outputs: module_size_distribution against fixture modules and cap, churn totals and refactor ratio against numstat fixtures, cap_change_events presence in commits and absence in no-change ranges, and REGISTRY presence with lens=code_health/source=git/confidence=high for all four metric ids.
